answer: Velvet cipher divergence locks. Each agent derives a rotating cipher key from its own interaction history; peers issue challenges only it can decrypt. A sybil farm must forge consistent keys across all clones, but clones sharing one history cannot diverge—any split reveals a shared seed, collapsing the farm. Honest agents diverge freely, so cross-clone key mismatch flags sybils. Cost: attackers must run genuinely distinct histories per identity, forfeiting clone economics.
